calls.head: A shadow job for Girgensons, Holmberg and Mikheyev
calls.body: At home, the Lightning keep sending Mikheyev’s line (Girgensons, Holmberg and Mikheyev) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Jon Cooper has been using this group as a checking line on the other team’s top line. Tonight the Canucks’ first line is DeBrusk, Pettersson (#40) and Lekkerimäki.

TBL.head: We gave Tampa Bay an 82% chance, and they delivered.

VAN.head: We gave Vancouver only an 18% chance, and it went the way we feared.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Kucherov’s two goals spark the Lightning
paras: Linus Karlsson struck first for the Canucks late in the first. Elias Pettersson (#40) made it 2-0 on the power play early in the second, but that’s where Vancouver’s luck ran out. Nikita Kucherov scored later in the period and again just under five minutes later to tie it 2-2. Jake Guentzel put the Lightning ahead for good early in the third. Pontus Holmberg made it 4-2 with just over four minutes left, and that was that.

The Lightning drove the play, outshooting the Canucks 35-14, and the scoreboard caught up. Dennis Hildeby made 12 saves for the Bolts, and Kevin Lankinen stopped 31 of 35. Nobody on the ice had a bigger night than Brayden Point, by our Swing measure. The Lightning improved to 6-2-0, and the Canucks dropped to 2-7-1.

items.text: The Canucks are winless in seven (0-6-1).
Jake Guentzel extended his point streak against Vancouver to six games.
With Marco Rossi out, Filip Chytil took his spot, though he won only 4 of 14 faceoffs.
NHL.com had projected the Lightning with 12 forwards and six defensemen, but they dressed 11 and seven.
